about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

corpus-map.json.note: #115 and #116 (docs/decisions/0026), on the map #117/#118 left (previousSha256). Five scope: out entries are added for Rules Glossary passages that modify in-slice rules (difficult-terrain-glossary, invisible-condition, cover-glossary, disengage-action) or the evidence of two existing ones is extended to the modifying sentence (incapacitated-condition, initiative-score-option); in-scope entries name them in crossReferences and dependsOn; flanking answers the pointer the SRD's new pointerPhrases detected. It changes relations and notes, so it carries an independent verdict. The reviewer saw only the corpus pages involved, a before/after of every changed entry, and the decision record; five rounds are recorded in the verdict file, the last two on the bytes re-applied after #117/#118 merged. previousReview is that earlier map's review, unchanged.

previousReview.note: #117 and #118 (docs/decisions/0025) added assertedBy to initiative-ties, gm-requires-action and sides-agree-to-end; draws to initiative-roll, group-initiative (with ambiguity.affectsDraws), attack-resolution and falling-off, each note quoting where the corpus names the die; and reconciled the initiative-ties and sides-agree-to-end notes. No other entry changed. It is a semantic change, so it carries an independent verdict and not an exemption. The verdict file names these bytes and records three rounds, the third on the map rebased onto #119. previousReview is #119's review (previousSha256), unchanged.

#113 and #114 (docs/decisions/0024), on the map the blind second mapping left (previousSha256). extent gains endsBefore "Damage and Healing"; six entries gain extraction {defect, renderedReading}; two notes stop pointing at the README for what those fields now carry. No entry's kind, scope, clarity, ambiguity, gates, evidence or citation changes. Everything but renderedReading is structure a check verifies (check-map.py extent and extraction; check-locators-pdf-text.py extent-end and extraction). renderedReading asserts what the printed page says, table values included, and nothing verifies it, so this is an independent verdict and not a non-semantic exemption: a reviewer in a separate context read the three distinct readings against renders of pp. 13-15 alone and agreed with all three. previousReview is that earlier map's review, unchanged.

Issue #106, step 3. compare.py read the map at 5216c62 (86 entries), the bytes the legacy exemption covered, and exits 1 unless each of its 259 flags has a row in resolutions.json. The map was corrected to those rows (21 blind-right, 11 corpus-does-not-settle; 91 entries) in the same commit that replaced the exemption with this review. sha256 is the corrected map; compared.sha256 is the map before correction. The blind mapper worked from docs with the SRD's name, combat vocabulary and the backgammon examples removed (blind-mapping/REDACTIONS.md), and from the corpus text and renders of pp. 13-16; what could not be ruled out, including that the mapper model knows this game, is in blind-mapping/README.md, Limits.
